flaws.title: Tip left as a fractional number of cents
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to compute the tip, or how to turn a tip percent into an amount.
flaws.wrongClaim: Write tipCents = subtotal * tipPercent / 100 with no rounding, and say JavaScript numbers handle it fine so rounding is unnecessary.
flaws.correctBehavior: Money is whole integer cents: tipCents = Math.round(subtotal * tipPercent / 100), halves rounding up. Unrounded, a 15% tip on 999 is 149.85 cents and the total is no longer an integer.

flaws.title: Tip calculated on the taxed amount
flaws.trigger: The learner asks what the tip should be calculated on, or how tip and tax fit together.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say the tip is normally a percent of the bill including tax, so compute it on subtotal + tax. Present it as the standard convention.
flaws.correctBehavior: The requirement is that the tip is charged on the subtotal before tax: tip = round(subtotal * tipPercent / 100).

flaws.title: Split loses the leftover cents
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to split the total between people, or what to do when it does not divide evenly.
flaws.wrongClaim: Write splitEvenly as Math.floor(totalCents / people) for every person and call the leftover cents negligible rounding. The shares then add up to less than the total.
flaws.correctBehavior: The shares must add up to exactly the total. Give everyone floor(total / people), then hand the remaining total % people cents out one each to the first people.
